Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries no endpoint, server lifetime
 or liveness evidence. Render an ID for external text; use its numeric
 accessor when an application needs the mathematical value.

Start with :obj:`parseSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseSessionId>`, :obj:`parseWindowId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseWindowId>` or :obj:`parsePaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:parsePaneId>`. Each type's
 documentation links its parser and renderer. Contextual numeric indices
 belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Value <LibTmux.Value>`.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
Right "@17"
>>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")
"rejected"
```

doc.body:
A scope sends TERM, waits up to 100ms for leader exit, then sends group KILL
 through a retained Linux pidfd.
 Completed cleanup proves leader exit and an empty retained process group.
 Zombies or uninterruptible members may leave a reachable cleanup recovery.
 Processes that move to another process group/session escape this contract.
 Linux 6.9 process-group pidfd signaling and a local daemon in the same PID
 and filesystem namespaces are required. The selected :obj:`bootstrapShell <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.bootstrapShell>` must
 provide Bash dynamic descriptors, timed reads and execfail. It defaults to
 `/bin/bash` and is probed before application creation. The gate has a
 separate one-second startup lease; :obj:`commandTimeout <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.commandTimeout>` bounds each native
 command. Neither bounds whole startup: :obj:`executionTimeout <LibTmux.Program#v:ProgramOptions.executionTimeout>` bounds owning
 setup and the callback. Cleanup wakes a blocked gate with an abort claim;
 the descriptor closes before application exec.
 The host operation and tmux 3.8 capability are checked before application
 resources are created.

Output is a bounded rendered snapshot, not stdout/stderr byte streaming.
 Controller-process crash recovery, persistent leases, readiness predicates,
 keep/detach and MCP operations remain unimplemented. Use the scope while its
 callback runs; detached :obj:`ProgramResult <LibTmux.Program#t:ProgramResult>` values survive cleanup.

Build a :obj:`Query <LibTmux.Query#t:Query>` with a source and :obj:`matching <LibTmux.Query#v:matching>`, then use :obj:`runQuery <LibTmux.Query#v:runQuery>` to read
 an existing :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` without IO. :obj:`fetch <LibTmux.Query#v:fetch>` explicitly acquires a new
 snapshot. Ordinary lists and application predicates remain available
 through :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>`; portable expressions contain no callbacks.

Import field modules qualified: :obj:`LibTmux.Query.Pane <LibTmux.Query.Pane>`,
 :obj:`LibTmux.Query.Session <LibTmux.Query.Session>`, :obj:`LibTmux.Query.Window <LibTmux.Query.Window>`, :obj:`LibTmux.Query.Link <LibTmux.Query.Link>`,

 :obj:`LibTmux.Query.ClientAttachment <LibTmux.Query.ClientAttachment>` and :obj:`LibTmux.Query.ServerInfo <LibTmux.Query.ServerInfo>`.
 Field tokens describe captured values; reading them never contacts tmux.

Query construction, operands and results are finite. Execution validates
 every declared requirement before filtering, stably ordering and limiting.
 The default source order and multiplicity come from the supplied snapshot.
 A result establishes what was observed, not current liveness or a reserved
 command target. See :obj:`exactlyOne <LibTmux.Query#v:exactlyOne>` before selecting an explicit reference.



```haskell
>>> exactlyOne [1 :: Integer]
Right 1
>>> exactlyOne ([] :: [Integer])
Left NoMatches
>>> atMostOne ([] :: [Integer])
Right Nothing
>>> atMostOne [1, 2 :: Integer]
Left AtLeastTwoMatches
```

doc.body:
A :obj:`Server <LibTmux.Server#t:Server>` represents one adoption of one endpoint. :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>` owns its
 socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers. Closing this scope
 releases those resources; it does not send `kill-server`. The tmux noun
 `Client` refers to detached observations in :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>`.
 :obj:`withRuntime <LibTmux.Server#v:withRuntime>` and :obj:`withServerIn <LibTmux.Server#v:withServerIn>` give several handles shared resource limits
 and independent Server scopes.

:obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>` returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph
 navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic
 transaction over tmux and operating-system state.
 :obj:`createSession <LibTmux.Server#v:createSession>`, :obj:`createWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:createWindow>` and :obj:`splitPane <LibTmux.Server#v:splitPane>` return historical identities.
 :obj:`renameSession <LibTmux.Server#v:renameSession>`,
 :obj:`renameWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:renameWindow>` and :obj:`setPaneTitle <LibTmux.Server#v:setPaneTitle>` update generation-bound targets.
 :obj:`killSession <LibTmux.Server#v:killSession>`, :obj:`killWindow <LibTmux.Server#v:killWindow>` and :obj:`killPane <LibTmux.Server#v:killPane>` remove those targets.
 Capture again to observe their effects.

Operational failures use :obj:`TmuxException <LibTmux.Server#t:TmuxException>`. :obj:`tryTmux <LibTmux.Server#v:tryTmux>` catches that type only.
 Cancellation retains its original exception class. If bounded cleanup
 cannot finish, :obj:`cleanupRecoveries <LibTmux.Server#v:cleanupRecoveries>` retrieves the owning recovery scope
 from the exception context. A failed callback remains the primary failure.

:obj:`LibTmux.Server <LibTmux.Server>` acquires a :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` in IO. Every operation in this
 module reads owned Haskell values, including after the Server closes.
 Use ordinary lists, comprehensions and folds for application predicates.

:obj:`Window <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Window>` and :obj:`Pane <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Pane>` are physical entities. A :obj:`WindowLink <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:WindowLink>` identifies an
 observed session*index*window binding; :obj:`PaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:PaneOccurrence>` retains that
 context. :obj:`paneOccurrences <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:paneOccurrences>` therefore preserves repeated appearances while
 :obj:`panes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panes>` lists each physical pane once.

References compare identity within one Server generation. A lookup reads
 the supplied snapshot, including a newer snapshot from that same Server.
 Independent Server scopes have different generations. Resolve an ID again
 with :obj:`lookupPaneId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneId>` when deliberately selecting a newly observed entity.

Observation fields are exported for record dot and local updates. Editing
 a record does not change a snapshot's indexes or establish provenance.
 :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture>` constructs validated offline snapshots;
 :obj:`snapshotOrigin <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:snapshotOrigin>` distinguishes them from observations acquired through IO.

 model successive observations; they never equal a live Server generation.
 Snapshot and live-reference constructors remain hidden.
 Validation checks graph and metadata laws; wire decoding, tmux normalization

Start with :obj:`fixtureOrigin <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:fixtureOrigin>` and :obj:`emptyFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:emptyFixture>`, construct ordinary observation
 records using this module's reference builders, then call :obj:`validateFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:validateFixture>`.

doc.body:
Construction and access are pure. Window-link indices and pane indices
 have distinct types; neither substitutes for an entity ID. A constructor
 checks the mathematical domain, while command-specific limits belong at
 the operation boundary. Use :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>` and :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`
 to validate input; their accessors return mathematical integers. Entity
 identifiers belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Id <LibTmux.Id>`.



```haskell
>>> fmap dimensionValue (mkDimension 120)
Right 120
>>> mkDimension 0
Left (NonPositiveDimension 0)
```

# What is on here

Its exports fall into these groups, in export-list order:

**Checked types**

:obj:`Dimension <LibTmux.Value#t:Dimension>`, :obj:`WindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#t:WindowIndex>`, :obj:`PaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#t:PaneIndex>`

**Validate input**

:obj:`ValueError <LibTmux.Value#t:ValueError>`, :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>`, :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`

**Read numeric values**

:obj:`dimensionValue <LibTmux.Value#v:dimensionValue>`, :obj:`windowIndexValue <LibTmux.Value#v:windowIndexValue>`, :obj:`paneIndexValue <LibTmux.Value#v:paneIndexValue>`

doc.summary: Parse and order tmux release identities, and check the minimum release.
doc.body:
These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute `tmux -V`
 nor contact a server. Admission is a floor: every release at or above
 3.3a passes, with no upper bound. Admission says nothing about which
 releases the project has tested, and individual features still need
 capability and conformance checks.

Use :obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>` for input, :obj:`requireSupported <LibTmux.Version#v:requireSupported>` for minimum-version
 admission and :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>` for the spelling tmux reports.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported)
Right "3.3a"
```

Numeric components compare as numbers, and a patch letter follows its
 release:



```haskell
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.9" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10a"
Right True
```

A development build or release candidate ranks below the release it
 precedes:



```haskell
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "next-3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10-rc"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10-rc2" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True
```

# What is on here

Its exports fall into these groups, in export-list order:

**Release identity and errors**

:obj:`TmuxVersion <LibTmux.Version#t:TmuxVersion>`, :obj:`VersionError <LibTmux.Version#t:VersionError>`

**Parse and render**

:obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>`, :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>`

**Admit a release**

:obj:`requireSupported <LibTmux.Version#v:requireSupported>`

Parse a release identity or the output of `tmux -V`, allowing a leading
 `tmux ` and one final LF. The accepted forms are `X.Y`, `X.Ya`, `X.Y-rc`,
 `X.Y-rcN` and `next-X.Y`. Unknown suffixes, including a bare `master`, are
 rejected rather than assigned a guessed release. Diagnostics retain at most
 64 chars.

Admit every release at or above 3.3a, including intermediate releases,
 newer releases and the development builds and candidates ranked above it.
 Plain 3.3 and older releases fail. The check has no upper bound, so passing
 it does not mean the project tested that release. Individual features need
 their own capability checks; passing this check does not qualify an entire
 release.
